top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B010) is the one proposal on the slate that rewards an identifiable discovery on common criteria. Melitz (2003) is a tractable model of selection into exporting, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extends it to exporting versus foreign investment. It explains newly documented firm-level facts: exporters are rare and systematically different, and liberalisation reallocates activity toward more productive firms. It generates predictions that representative-firm trade theory does not, so it is distinct from the 2008 recognition. These predictions have been tested on firm-level data in many countries for over twenty years, so maturity is not in doubt. The two-name credit follows the intellectual structure. The main costs are the uncredited precursors (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum, Hopenhayn) and the dependence of welfare magnitudes on distributional assumptions, which citation wording and the scientific background can handle. I base this on my own recollection of the literature, not on verified sources. Broad agreement among members is evidence of stable attribution, not of merit. A no-award outcome would withhold a prize from a mature, well-tested contribution, so P000 is ranked last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to Helpman or Melitz. My frequent co-authors (Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner, Bindler) are not credited on this proposal. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
